note: Generated once and committed. Seeding is offline and deterministic.

generic: Called in 9.20am, quick one. {contact} on site at the Ashgrove Road plots so spoke to Karen in the office instead, nothing needed this week.
Steve Ogden is the one placing most of the orders now, Dave only does the big stuff. Worth getting Steve's mobile on the system.
Usual monthly run of insulation going out, 60 sheets of 50mm PIR last drop. No change expected.
Mentioned they've got the Willow Bank extension starting mid March, three units, should be steady kitchen and joinery pulls off the back of it.
Nothing doing today, just a coffee and a catch up. Account ticking along, no complaints raised.
Karen in accounts asked for invoices to go to the ap@ address rather than the general inbox. Sorted with credit control after.
They still prefer next day on timber rather than holding stock, yard space is tight behind the workshop.
{contact} says the lads get through PPE faster in winter, gloves mainly. Suggested a bulk box, he'll think about it.
Quiet visit. Site vans all out, only the apprentice in. Left a price list and my card.
Dave Pritchard's lad has just started at Loughborough doing quantity surveying, he was pleased as punch about it. Ask next time.
Ordering pattern is very predictable, Tuesday and Thursday most weeks, deliveries booked for 7am starts.
Had a look at the {category} range with them, no urgency but they said keep them posted on any deals.
Van driver Wayne gets on well with their yard man, worth keeping that pairing on the route.
Nothing to report really. Same faces, same jobs, account healthy and paying on time.
Their forklift is on its last legs by the sound of it but that's their problem, just means they want palletised stuff broken down where possible.
Talked through drainage for the Priory Lane job, 110mm underground, they'll come back with quantities once groundworks confirm.
{competitor} rep has been in but only for plumbing bits, {contact} said he's not interested in switching the main account.
Steve mentioned they're two weeks behind on the Meadow Close job because of the weather. Nothing that affects us.
Left a couple of samples of the new sealant, he'll try one tube and let me know.
Very easy account to deal with, no drama in three years. Just needs a face every six weeks or so.
Prices on plasterboard queried lightly, more of a grumble than anything. Explained the market, he was fine with it.
They do their own collections on small bits, usually Friday afternoons in the crew cab.
Karen off on holiday first two weeks of August, cover is Jenny in the office. Note for invoice queries.
Asked about a trade account for their subbie sparky. Said I'd send the form over but not chasing it.
Good relationship here. {contact} always makes time, offers a brew, but doesn't want a long visit.
Fixings and consumables all coming through us, timber split with someone else historically but that's dropped off.
Nothing new. Confirmed delivery address for the Ashgrove site is via the Cotton Lane entrance, not the main gate.
He wants a call rather than an email if there's ever a shortage. Doesn't check email till evening.
Bagged aggregates moving steadily, roughly 40 bags a fortnight through the summer months.
Mentioned in passing they might take on another bricklayer. Nothing confirmed.
Site tidy, well run. Gives me confidence they'll keep paying.
{contact} played golf at Cavendish over the weekend, took a bit of a hiding by the sound of it. Small talk for next time.
Waiting on a quote back from me for roofing membrane, promised it by Friday. Not urgent for them but I said I'd do it.
They've been with us since the old branch manager's day, loyalty is strong. Don't take it for granted though.
Quick doorstep visit, five minutes. All fine, reorder same as last month.
Dave asked whether we do hire. Told him no, but pointed him at Barnfield down the road. He appreciated it.
No credit issues, terms are 30 days end of month and they've never gone past it.
Their storage container at Priory Lane is getting emptied so expect a small top up order on hand tools.
Steve prefers the delivery notes signed by whoever's on site, not left in the van. Passed to transport.
Nothing significant this visit, just keeping the relationship warm. Next call in six weeks.
He said skirting and architrave from us has been good quality lately, no returns. Worth telling the branch.
Volume flat year on year which is fine given how quiet the trade has been round here.
Might be worth showing them the {category} promo when it lands, they're open minded but not chasers of deals.
Reminder to self, don't call Monday mornings, that's when they do their week's planning and he's short.
All in all a solid, unspectacular account. No risk flags, no growth opportunity screaming out, just keep servicing it properly.
Called in 10.15, saw Dave Pritchard the yard manager, nothing much doing, usual monthly top up on fixings and sealants. All fine.
{contact} happy enough with service, no issues raised. Just ticking along on the same order pattern as last quarter.
Quick one today, only had ten minutes as they were loading out. Said to ring Thursday morning if I need anything.
Stock check on their consumables shelf - down to about half on 100mm bright screws, they'll order Friday same as always.
Sue in accounts confirmed the paperwork is all up to date, no queries outstanding. Nice and clean account.
Talked through the plasterboard prices, no change wanted, happy with where we are. They're not shopping around as far as I can tell.
Weather's slowed them a bit this week, groundworks lads stood down Tuesday. Doesn't affect their ordering much, they buy monthly regardless.
Left a copy of the new drainage brochure with {contact}, said he'd have a flick through. Nothing pressing.
Rang ahead but ended up popping in anyway. Kev was on the trade counter, said the last three deliveries all landed on time.
They've got a small extension job starting Mowbray Road in about three weeks, standard footings and blockwork. Nothing we don't already supply them.
Note for next time - Dave's off on holiday first two weeks of August, Gary Kemp covers the ordering.
No movement on {category} with these, they still buy that elsewhere out of habit. Not worth pushing hard, just mention it now and then.
Very steady account, same spend most months, no drama. Just needs a visit every six weeks to keep the face known.
Asked about pallet returns, they've got about twelve stacked round the back. Booked a collection on next delivery.
Chatted football for ten minutes, Dave's a Barnsley fan and suffering. Worth remembering.
Their van fleet is three Transits, all sign written, mainly domestic work within 20 miles. Nothing changing there.
Order went in for 40 bags of postcrete and a bundle of 3x2 CLS, delivery Wednesday. Straightforward.
New lad started with them, Ryan, second year apprentice. Introduced myself, showed him the counter side of things.
No credit issues, they pay to terms every month without chasing. Sue does it on the 28th like clockwork.
{competitor} rep was in last Tuesday apparently, left a price list. Dave didn't seem bothered either way.
Talked about the timber market, they've accepted prices are where they are. No complaints, just gets on with it.
Bit quiet in the yard when I got there, only two customers on site. Said trade's normal for the time of year.
Reminded them about the trade day in June, said they'd try to send someone. Not holding my breath but it's on their radar.
Checked the PPE cupboard, decent stock of gloves but low on size 10 boots. Will drop a pair of samples in next time.
Nothing to report really. In and out in fifteen, all good, next call mid month.
They use a Belle mixer that's on its last legs, Dave joked about replacing it. Could be a small hire or sale opportunity later in the year.
Delivery went to the wrong gate last month but they sorted it themselves, didn't even ring us. Worth a word with transport anyway.
Gary mentioned they might take on a fourth van later in the year if the work holds. Nothing firm.
Talked through our own brand sealants vs what they're using. Not interested in switching mid job, said maybe next order.
{contact} asked for a copy of the current price file emailed over. Sent it from the van before I drove off.
Site at Fenton Way is nearly finished, last of the render going on. Nothing more needed from us on that one.
Cash flow fine, no requests for extended terms. Never had one from this account.
Popped in with a box of doughnuts for the lads, always goes down well here. Good rapport, easy visit.
They buy a lot of 25kg sand and ballast, roughly a pallet a fortnight. Consistent for the last two years.
Nothing new on the account. Same contacts, same products, same volumes. Happy customer.
Mentioned the delivery cut off moving to 3pm, {contact} said no problem, they order the day before anyway.
Discussed a small bulk deal on 110mm underground pipe, he wants to think about storage space first. Follow up in a month.
Dave's daughter is getting married in September, he'll be off for a bit around then. Diary it.
Asked whether they wanted a quote for the scaffold boards, said they hire those in. Not a line for us here.
Nothing controversial, no complaints, no compliments either. Just a solid, quiet account that runs itself.
Their storage unit off Aldersgate Lane is fairly tight, so they prefer smaller more frequent drops. Keep deliveries to half pallets where possible.
Went through last six months spend with Kev, up very slightly on the year before. Both agreed that's about right for their size.
Left my mobile again as they'd lost the old card. Said to text orders direct if the counter's busy.
Feels like a decent account to leave well alone. Regular contact, no pushing, they'll come to us when they need it.
Next visit planned for week commencing the 14th, morning is best, they're out on sites after 11.
healthy: Called in 9:15, {contact} on the trade counter phone but waved me through. All good, no issues raised, order book looking healthy.
Dave Enright (contracts manager) has taken on the Kirkstall Road flats phase 2, 34 plots, starts mid March. Wants a call on plasterboard and metal stud nearer the time.
Steady month again, up about 8% on same period last year by their reckoning. Nothing broken so I didn't push.
Left the new insulation brochure with Kelly on reception, she'll put it in Dave's tray. Sausage roll offered, accepted.
They've bought a second Manitou telehandler, second hand off a Doncaster dealer. Yard is getting tight now, mentioned they may need to look at storage racking.
Quick one, 20 mins. Confirmed Thursday deliveries suit them best, before 10 if possible as the gang travel from Halifax.
{contact} said our driver Ronnie is the reason they stick with us, always rings ahead and never leaves pallets in the mud. Passed that on to transport.
Talked through the {category} range extension. Interested but not urgent, said come back after Easter when the new unit is up and running.
Site visit at Ackworth with their foreman Gary Pilkington. Blocks stacked neat, our labels everywhere, no competitor product visible on site at all.
Cashflow fine, they pay to terms without chasing. Credit control had them flagged for a review, told Sue in accounts they're safe to increase the limit.
They're quoting a school refurb in Wakefield, decision due end of April. Asked me for indicative pricing on suspended ceiling grid and tiles.
Nothing much to report, just a face to face to keep warm. Two coffees and a chat about the rugby.
New estimator started, Priya Chauhan, ex {competitor} so she knows the market. Worth building a relationship there, she'll be doing all the take offs.
Asked about our hire desk. They currently go local for breakers and floor saws but would consider us if we can do same day.
Bought their first pallet of the porcelain paving, sold through in a fortnight. Reordered two more, said the homeowners love the grey.
{contact} mentioned his daughter's wedding in July, taking two weeks off around it. Make sure someone else is briefed before then.
Delivery went to the wrong gate at the Selby job last week. They laughed it off but let's not repeat, gate details now on the account notes.
Head count up to 14 from 11 last year. Two new apprentices through the CITB route, both on site with Gary.
Went through the timber pricing, they accept the increases as long as we give a week's notice. Fair enough, no pushback.
Big spend on fixings and consumables this quarter, higher than usual. Suspect they're stocking their own van store rather than buying weekly.
Yard manager Wes says the strapping on the last block delivery was slack, two courses shifted. Minor, but flagged to the depot.
They've registered for the new build framework with the housing association. If it lands it's a step up in volume, worth watching from June.
Happy customer, genuinely. Said we're easier to deal with than their old supplier and they've no reason to look elsewhere.
Discussed a stock and call off arrangement for aggregates on the Ackworth job. Sending proposal for 40 tonne calls off across 6 weeks.
Their van livery is new, looks smart. Small thing but they're clearly investing.
{contact} asked whether we do the trade rewards points scheme, didn't know we had it. Signed him up, he's keen on the tool vouchers.
Popped in unannounced, {contact} out on site. Left card with the counter lad, will catch him Tuesday.
Doing more groundworks than before, less first fix carpentry. Might explain the shift in mix towards drainage and concrete products.
Long chat about labour shortages, can't get plasterers for love nor money. Nothing for us to sell there but good to know their constraints.
Sample of the composite decking left with them for the Otley bungalow extension. Client picking colour end of next week.
Order value per drop is climbing, average around 1,400 now against 900 last spring. Sensible growth, not a spike.
They store nothing on site overnight since the theft at their Pontefract job in November. All deliveries need to be timed for a man being there.
Mentioned {competitor} rep has been in twice this year. {contact} says he's polite but keeps quoting on things they don't buy.
Gary is doing his SSSTS in March, asked if we run any toolbox talk style training. Might be worth the manufacturer rep doing a session.
Their office is above a chippy on Bridge Street, parking is a nightmare. Note to self, use the Co-op car park and walk round.
Reviewed last 12 months spend together, no surprises for either of us. Agreed to keep the same rebate structure for another year.
Asked for a copy of the fire door datasheet, building control chasing them on the Leeds conversion. Emailed same afternoon.
Good rapport now, we're past the formal stage. He rings me direct rather than the branch when something's urgent.
Concrete lintels are the one line they buy elsewhere, purely on lead time. If we can get to 48 hours we'd win it.
Quiet fortnight coming as they've a gap between jobs. Expect the order rate to dip briefly then pick up from the 20th.
Talked through EV charging install work, they're getting asked about it more. Not our area really but I said I'd find out what we stock.
They've bought a small yard off the bypass, exchange next month. Means proper storage and bigger drops, potentially full loads.
{contact} is a Leeds season ticket holder, east stand. Worth an invite to the hospitality day if we get tickets.
No complaints, no queries, no returns in three months. Almost suspiciously smooth, but I think they're just well run.
Left the new catalogue and the drainage price list. He flicked through and said the manhole cover range looks better than before.
Overall a solid account that looks after itself. Monthly visit is enough, don't over service it, just keep the relationship warm.
Called in on Dave Whitlock, buyer, all good. Order book solid through to March, no complaints on service or delivery.
Yard was rammed when I got there, two vans loading at once. Told me they've taken on another fitter starting Monday.
{contact} happy with the switch to the Hanson bagged cement, says less waste than the last lot. Worth pushing the rest of the range.
Picked up on a new build at Chorley Old Road, 14 units. They're doing first fix from mid Feb, plumbing and insulation will come through us.
No issues raised at all this visit. Just a coffee and a catch up, keep the cadence at monthly.
Steve in the office mentioned they're outgrowing the unit at Farnworth. Looking at a bigger yard within 12 months, might mean a bulk storage conversation.
Talked timber. They're taking around 40 sheets of 18mm OSB a month now, up from about 25 last year.
Left a copy of the new {category} brochure with Jan on reception, she'll get it to Dave.
Good rapport, easy visit. Been buying off us six years and says he's never had to chase a delivery.
They quoted a school refurb in Rochdale, find out in three weeks. Would be a decent chunk of plasterboard and metal stud if it lands.
Mark the foreman asked about the DeWalt promo, wants the 18v combi kit. Sent him the deal sheet after.
Account trending up, spend well ahead of same period last year. Nothing to fix, just keep showing face.
Mentioned {competitor} rep has been in twice. Not worried, {contact} said prices were nowhere near.
Their van driver Kev broke his wrist, off for six weeks. May need more of their stuff delivered rather than collected in the meantime.
Discussed monthly statements, they'd prefer them emailed to accounts@ rather than posted. Passed to credit control.
New apprentice, Ryan, doing the collections. Told trade counter to look after him and not let him take the wrong beads again.
Site visit at Bury, they're on the roof of a warehouse conversion. Talked single ply and edge trim, sending over spec Thursday.
Nice steady account. No drama, pays on time, orders in a rhythm. Don't over engineer it.
{contact} off to Lanzarote for a fortnight from the 8th. Steve covering ordering, worth a call in that window.
They've started doing more groundworks off their own bat. Opportunity on drainage and MOT type 1 if we can get the haulage right.
Talked through the new online ordering portal, he's keen but wants a walkthrough. Booked in for the 22nd, 9am at their office.
Spend sitting around 4k a month, very consistent. Credit limit at 6k, may want lifting before spring.
Asked about pallet returns, they've got about 20 stacked up. Arranged collection with transport for next Tuesday.
Good news, they landed the care home job at Whitefield. Starts April, ten week programme.
Bit of a moan about the trade counter queue on Saturday mornings. Not a real issue but worth flagging to branch.
They're loyal to Marshalls on paving, won't be moved. Fine, we supply it anyway, just don't push alternatives.
{contact}'s lad plays for Bolton Wanderers under 14s, mentions it every visit. Ask how he got on.
Fixings spend is lower than it should be for their volume. Suspect they're picking up screws and anchors locally, chase it.
Left samples of the composite decking. Doing a couple of garden jobs in summer, could be a new line for them.
All invoices clear, nothing overdue. Accounts lady Sue said the new remittance format is much easier.
They want a price on 200 lengths of 47x100 C24 for the Radcliffe job. Quote due back by Friday.
Easy going relationship, {contact} takes my calls first time. Don't waste that, only ring when there's something worth saying.
Noticed they've bought a second Transit tipper. Growth is real, not just talk.
Talked about a stock holding arrangement on their regular insulation sizes. Interested but wants to see the numbers.
Asked me to sort a returns credit on the wrong door linings. Raised it same day, credit due through this week.
They're pushing into loft conversions this year. Steels, joists and Velux, worth getting the Velux rep alongside me on the next call.
Yard is tidy, kit is looked after, staff seem settled. Well run outfit, low risk.
Dropped off a couple of hoodies and a site radio. Went down well, Mark had it on the bench before I left.
Nothing needed this visit. Quick ten minutes, order placed for delivery Wednesday am, before 10 as always.
They've asked whether we do hire. Pointed them at the plant desk, could be a decent bolt on for them.
Payment terms 30 days end of month, never late. Would support an extension if they ask when the bigger jobs land.
{contact} rates our driver Barry, says he backs into their yard better than anyone. Little thing but it keeps them with us.
Discussed the price increase letter coming in April. Took it well, just wants a heads up on the timber lines specifically.
Growth is steady rather than spiky, about 12 percent up year on year. Sensible operators, they don't overreach.
Next visit end of March. Bring the tool promo, the portal login sorted, and a price on the Radcliffe timber package.
Called in at 9am, {contact} on the phone to a supplier but waved me through, said trade's been solid all quarter and no complaints on service.
Karl Deeming, yard foreman, wants the 8am drop kept as is - says anything later and his lads are stood about. Passed to transport to protect that slot.
They've picked up the barn conversion at Nether Fenley, 14 week programme starting mid March. Should be decent timber and insulation pull-through.
Spend up again on last quarter, mostly driven by {category}. Nothing to fix here, just keep showing up.
{contact} mentioned his lad Ryan starts his apprenticeship in September, wants him on the account for collections. Told him I'd sort a card.
Quoted 62 sheets of 12.5mm standard board plus scrim and beads for the Ashwell Road flats. Expect the order Thursday.
Nice easy visit. Coffee in the portacabin, half an hour of football, no issues raised at all.
They've taken on two more bricklayers since Christmas, now running three gangs. Volume should follow.
Warned him prices on rebar are moving in April. He took it well, said he'd rather know early than get a shock on the invoice.
Sharon in their office is the one who actually places the orders - {contact} just signs things off. Need to build that relationship more, I've been ignoring her.
Left a sample of the new hybrid sealant. He's used the old one for years so it's a slow sell but worth a try.
They're at about 60 percent of credit limit most months now. Worth flagging to finance for an uplift before it becomes a problem.
Groundworks side growing faster than the build side. Chambers, pipe and bedding stone all up.
{contact} away in Lanzarote first two weeks of August. Deal with Sharon or Karl in that window.
Talked through the fixings deal. He's happy with pricing, said {competitor} rang him last month and he didn't even bother getting them in.
New Transit tipper on the fleet, sign written. Business is clearly going well, he was pleased with himself about it.
Site visit at Hollow Lane with Martin Kelso, the site manager. Very tidy operation, everything stacked and covered. Easy to deliver to.
Asked about our hire book - might want a 1.5t excavator for a fortnight in May. Sent the rates over the same day.
Small gripe about a short delivery on sand back in Feb, sorted at the time, he only mentioned it in passing. Nothing to act on.
They're going after more housing association repairs work. If they land it there'll be steady small-order volume, kitchens and bathrooms.
Dropped off the new insulation guide and a stack of catalogues for the counter at their unit.
{contact} is a Grimsby Town fan, season ticket. Useful bit of small talk, he lights up.
Order for 40 lengths of 110mm underground and 6 inspection chambers going in for the Cotters Field job.
Everything about this account is quiet in a good way. No chasing, no arguments, pays on the nail.
Third quarter running they've beaten the same period last year. Steady rather than spiky, which I prefer.
He's thinking about a small trade counter at the front of their unit for the local sparks and plumbers. Long shot but I'd like to supply it if it happens.
Mentioned they trialled a couple of pallets from {competitor} on aggregates purely on price. Said the service was poor and he won't repeat it.
Dean the driver knows their yard well now, gets in and out with no fuss. Worth keeping him on the run.
PPE spend has crept up with the extra lads. Suggested a standing monthly order for gloves, hi vis and safety boots.
Roofing enquiry come in - slate for a farmhouse near Braithwood. Passed to Gavin in the specialist team.
{contact}'s wife had a knee operation in January, all fine now. Remember to ask.
They want everything on one consolidated statement rather than per site. Told accounts, should be sorted from next month.
Talked rebate. He knows he's close to the next threshold and is actively steering spend our way to hit it. Good sign.
Bought their first cordless SDS off us instead of the shed. Small thing but he's shifting more of his tool spend across.
Extension job on Willow Drive finishing next week, snagging only. Nothing more needed from us on that one.
Nothing raised, nothing wrong. Sometimes the best visits are the ones where you just have a brew and go.
He's tight on yard space at the unit, so wants call-off deliveries rather than one big drop. Explained we can hold stock for them.
Bagged cement usage up sharply, now taking a pallet a fortnight rather than a month.
Karl asked about a mixer forks attachment for the telehandler. Sent him a link, might be a hire not a sale.
Quiet warning sign - he mentioned a main contractor is 60 days behind paying them. Watch the ledger even though it's clean now.
They've booked in for the manufacturer's day at the depot in October. {contact} and two of the lads coming.
New estimator started, Priya Chandran, comes from a plumbing merchant background. Introduced myself, should be a good contact for pricing enquiries.
Landed the drainage schedule for phase two off the back of us getting phase one out on time. Service is genuinely winning here.
He likes a text rather than a call, replies within minutes. Stopped ringing him and it's improved things.
Overall a really comfortable account. Growing, loyal, no drama - just needs regular contact so nobody else gets a foot in.
Called in 9.20am, Dave Whitlock (yard manager) says timber offtake up again on last month, mainly C16 4x2 for the Kingsmead estate.
Quick one, all fine, nothing needed. Said he'd ring if the plasterboard run gets tight.
{contact} mentioned they've taken on two more vans, so delivery windows may need looking at. Nothing urgent but worth flagging to transport.
Sharon on the trade counter asked if we can start splitting the invoices by site ref - they're running three jobs now and accounts is getting in a muddle. Passed to Lisa in credit control.
Went through the new fixings range with them, took a starter deal on the 100 box multipack. Trial order only but he seemed keen.
Good chat about the extension they're pricing in Nantwich, 40 plus plots, decision end of Q3. Worth staying close.
They're happy. Genuinely nothing to fix here, just keep turning up.
Left a copy of the insulation price list. Currently buying most of that elsewhere out of habit rather than price, so there's a gap for us.
Steve's lad Callum has started in the business, doing buying two days a week. Make sure he gets on the mailing list and knows who to ring.
Order pattern very steady, Tuesday and Thursday deliveries, they like the same driver. Barry apparently. Don't mess with it.
Mentioned {competitor} have been in twice this month with a rep chasing the drainage. He wasn't interested but they are sniffing round.
Site visit at the Longridge Road job, decent size, three storey block. They're using our blocks all the way through which is nice to see.
Asked about hire - they're renting a mini digger weekly from someone local. Might be an opportunity if we can get the rates right.
Nice and relaxed visit, coffee and a moan about the weather. No issues raised at all.
Talked through the {category} range extension. He'll look at it properly after the bank holiday, said ring him week of the 12th.
Turnover tracking about 15 percent up year on year on this account by my reckoning. Nothing dramatic, just consistent.
He wants a quote on 60 lengths of 110 underground pipe plus bends for the Tarvin job. Promised it by Friday.
{contact} off on holiday to Portugal the last two weeks of July, Gary covering. Don't chase anything in that window.
Been buying more of the power tool accessories since we sorted the display. Small money but it's sticky business.
Nothing to report other than they're busy. Two skips in the yard and a full board of jobs on the wall.
Reminded him about the loyalty rebate threshold, he's about 8k off it with four months to run. He reckons they'll walk it.
Their storeman Pete is a proper stickler for delivery notes being signed correctly. Make sure the drivers know.
Quick doorstep chat, he was on the phone the whole time. Rebook properly for next month.
They've moved to paying by direct debit which accounts will be pleased about. No more chasing.
Asked whether we do anything on PPE workwear with logos embroidered. Said I'd find out - they'd want around 20 fleeces.
Sensible outfit, well run, pay on time. The sort of account you don't want to take for granted.
Discussed the sealant and adhesives lines, they're loyal to one brand but open to a comparison if the price is right.
He's flagged that the last two loads came slightly short on cement and had to be topped up. Not cross about it but twice now, worth watching.
New unit on the industrial estate at Sandbach signed off, moving in October. More storage means bigger drops.
Personal note - his wife Karen runs the accounts side from home, always polite on the phone. Send a Christmas card to both.
Rang ahead but he was on site so I went out to him, muddy boots job. Good rapport, he likes that we come out to the work rather than sitting in the office.
Went over Q1 spend versus last year, up in every category except roofing which is flat. Roofing worth a look.
He commented that our online ordering is easier than the last lot he used. Small thing but he brought it up unprompted.
Asked me for a favour on a one-off, needed 12 sheets of OSB same day. Sorted it through the branch, he was grateful. Bank that.
Overall no risk here, just needs regular contact and the odd new line put in front of them. Next visit six weeks.
declining: Popped in Tues morning, Dave was on the phone to a QS sounding fed up. Two of the four jobs he had penciled in for spring have gone quiet.
Spend down again this month, roughly half what he was doing this time last year. He knows it, I know it, neither of us made a big thing of it.
Wharf Lane plots 6 to 9 are on hold until the developer sorts the drainage adoption. That was his bread and butter through the winter.
Karen in the office says they've stopped ordering ahead and are buying week to week now. Worth quoting tighter on the regular lines.
He's still got the Beeston care home extension running but it's small beer, two lads on it and it finishes end of April.
Asked about our timber prices unprompted, which he never used to do. Price sensitivity has definitely crept in.
Mentioned {competitor} rang him twice last week offering free delivery under £250. He didn't sound tempted but he did remember the number.
Sean the foreman was in the yard, said they've laid off one of the agency lads and the other is down to three days.
Still buying all his plasterboard off us, that hasn't shifted. Insulation is where the volume has dropped off a cliff.
Bit of frustration about a short delivery before Christmas that nobody rang him about. Said it politely but he brought it up again unasked, so it's still sitting with him.
Good rapport still there, he made me a brew and we talked about Forest for twenty minutes. Relationship is fine, it's the workload that's the problem.
Longmoor Road barn conversion is the one live enquiry, private client, slow to sign. He reckons June start if it happens at all.
Told him about the account rebate tiers and he laughed, said he'd struggle to hit tier one this year. Fair point, don't push that again.
Van is looking tired, the Transit has done 190k and he said he can't justify changing it yet.
Ordering pattern has gone from Monday morning bulk to little drips on a Thursday. Watch that, usually means cash is tight.
He's chasing £14k off a developer that's 90 days overdue. That's the real reason spend is down, not lack of loyalty.
Ryan the apprentice is doing his level 2 at West Notts, Dave's paying for it himself. Nice detail, ask next visit.
Asked if we do sale or return on unopened boards. We don't but I said I'd check, need to come back to him either way.
Doing a lot more small domestic now, bathrooms and loft conversions, so basket size has shrunk but frequency is holding up.
Sand and cement still going out steady. It's the {category} spend that's evaporated.
He was blunt about credit limit, said he doesn't need more, he needs jobs. Don't lead with finance next time.
Rang ahead, he'd rather I turn up unannounced Tuesday or Thursday mornings. Fridays he's on site.
Wife Michelle does the books two days a week since they let the bookkeeper go. Small firm getting smaller.
